page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.96xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors delivering 384 vCPUs across 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.9 GHz. The compute topology is backed by an extensive cache hierarchy including 480 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). Memory configuration consists of 3072.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 RAM at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Storage and network subsystems are scaled to accommodate enterprise data volumes without separate external attachments. The instance includes 22,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage directly attached for low-latency operations. Complementing local I/O, networking infrastructure provides up to 400 Gbps of baseline bandwidth. Acceleration relies entirely on CPU instruction sets, as no dedicated discrete GPUs are included in this instance type.

Empirical benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities across parallel compute and data throughput. In stress-ng testing, multi-core throughput registered 413,592.34 in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, despite single-core output placing in the middle 50 percent. Memory bandwidth reached 1,128.02 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 454.14 GB/sec for writes. The platform demonstrated exceptional performance on in-memory caching and compression, recording 494.73 million operations per second on Redis SET operations, 1,891.25 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and 159.43 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an architectural tradeoff perspective, the massive core density and 3 TB of DDR5 offer high resource density, making it cost-efficient for consolidation of large-scale in-memory databases and high-concurrency analytics over deploying fragmented nodes. However, sequential single-threaded execution remains moderate, and without discrete GPU acceleration, text generation for large language models remains constrained. The configuration is primarily aligned with memory-bound workloads, massive in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, and high-throughput data processing pipelines requiring extensive local NVMe scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idb.96xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro instance powered by 384 vCPUs from Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors with 480 MB of L3 cache and AMX acceleration. The system pairs 3072.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory with 22,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Evaluated performance exhibits top-tier multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory read bandwidth of 1,128.02 GB/sec, and 494.73 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. While single-thread speeds are standard and discrete GPUs are absent, the dense 3 TB memory pool, extensive NVMe scratch capacity, and high network throughput make this instance a targeted platform for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, and high-volume data analytics engines.
